scale.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 10^9 as "ena milijarda" and 10^12 as "en bilijon": Slovene counts in the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a dot.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the decimal symbol is a comma.

space_groups.source: CLDR common/main/sl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a dot, not a space, so a space between digit strings separates two numbers.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF sl writes a plural scale word only after its count ("dva tisoč", 2000). A plural scale word with no count names an amount, not a number. Slovene "tisoč" does not change after a count, so only "milijoni", "milijarde" and the like are plural.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF sl %spellout-cardinal-masculine renders 10^6, 2 x 10^6, 5 x 10^6 and 21 x 10^6 as "en milijon", "dva milijona", "pet milijonov", "enegaindvajset milijonov": the scale noun takes the number and case its count governs. The scale words of this lexicon are scale_numeral entries whose plural flag carries that agreement.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF sl: "20: [>%spellout-cardinal-masculine-accusative>in]dvajset;": Slovene puts the unit before the ten, read by inverted_tens; a ten never takes "in" before a unit after it.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 345 as "tristo petinštirideset", no conjunction after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 1001 as "tisoč en", no conjunction between groups.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 1100 as "tisoč sto" and 1500 as "tisoč petsto": no joiner stands before a round hundred after the thousands.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 21 in %spellout-ordinal-masculine as "enegaindvajseti": only the last part is ordinal.

compound_words.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 345 as "tristo petinštirideset", with the hundreds and the tens each one word, and 2000th as "dvatisoči". A word that is a sequence of number words reads as its parts.

inverted_tens.source: CLDR RBNF sl: "20: [>%spellout-cardinal-masculine-accusative>in]dvajset;": the unit, then "in", then the ten, in one word.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Slovene has no article, so a singular collective or fraction noun alone counts one. Slovar slovenskega knjižnega jezika (SSKJ², Fran), "tretjina": "del na tri enake dele razdeljene celote".

decimal_fractions.source: CLDR RBNF sl renders 2.5 as "dve celi pet", with the decimal digits as a cardinal; this lexicon has no read source for a power-of-ten fraction after "celi".

joiner.source: CLDR RBNF sl: "20: [>%spellout-cardinal-masculine-accusative>in]dvajset;": "in" joins the unit to the ten. "in" also joins a half to a whole: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

minus_idioms.source: This lexicon lists no Slovene idiom that puts "minus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: Slovene has no article; "en" is a numeral.

of.source: Slovene marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

fraction_of.source: Slovene marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

denominator_particle.source: Slovene has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Slovene names no digit class with a singular noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: The half "pol" is its own word before the unit, read by the half role: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

abbreviation.source: No Slovene number word in this lexicon is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sl.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae): the decimal symbol is a comma; a comma before the first digit marks decimals.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary (en), "med": "between", used in the structure "med X in Y"; "in" joins the two limits, so it ends the first number.
